title: Geometry - Lesson 10 Assessment: Cumulative Map Reasoning
description: Show mastery by planning a geometric map, identifying relationships, solving missing angle measures, and explaining each step.

questions.question: Which set of features best matches the Lesson 10 construction task?
options: Parallel roads, a perpendicular road, a transversal, labels, angle measures, and reasons
Only one line segment and its midpoint
A circle with no angle labels
A table of numbers with no diagram
questions.explanation: The cumulative task requires a map that uses parallel and perpendicular roads, a transversal, labels, solved angle measures, and organized reasoning.

questions.question: Roads $m$ and $n$ are parallel. A transversal creates $m\angle 1 = 66^\circ$. Which measure must be true for the corresponding angle?
questions.explanation: Corresponding angles formed by parallel lines are congruent, so the corresponding angle is $66^\circ$.

questions.question: An angle in a same-side interior pair measures $41^\circ$. What is the measure of the other same-side interior angle?
questions.explanation: Same-side interior angles are supplementary, so the other angle is $180^\circ - 41^\circ = 139^\circ$.

questions.question: If $p \perp q$, then the angles formed where $p$ and $q$ intersect are right angles.
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines intersect to form right angles, each measuring $90^\circ$.

questions.question: If one angle in a linear pair measures $128^\circ$, the other angle measures ______ degrees.
questions.explanation: Linear pair angles sum to $180^\circ$, so $180 - 128 = 52$.

questions.question: Which reason best justifies the statement $m\angle 4 = m\angle 6$ when the angles are alternate interior angles formed by parallel roads?
options: Alternate interior angles are congruent when lines are parallel
All angles in a diagram are equal
questions.explanation: When parallel lines are cut by a transversal, alternate interior angles are congruent.

questions.question: A road crossing two parallel roads is called a ______.
questions.explanation: A transversal intersects two or more lines, including two parallel roads in a map diagram.

questions.question: Write a short construction plan for a map that includes two parallel roads, one perpendicular road, and one transversal.
questions.correctAnswer: Draw road a, then construct road b parallel to a. Draw road c crossing both a and b as a transversal. Construct road d perpendicular to road a and label the intersections and angles.
questions.explanation: A strong plan names the relationships first, then adds labels so the map can be checked.

questions.question: A student claims two same-side interior angles are both $82^\circ$ because the roads are parallel. Correct the mistake.
questions.correctAnswer: Same-side interior angles formed by parallel lines are supplementary, not congruent. If one is $82^\circ$, the other is $98^\circ$ because $180 - 82 = 98$.
questions.explanation: The correction must name the relationship and use subtraction from $180^\circ$.

questions.question: In a final map solution, why is it not enough to list angle answers without reasons?
questions.correctAnswer: Geometry solutions need reasons so another person can verify that each measure follows from a relationship such as a linear pair, vertical angles, corresponding angles, or perpendicular lines.
questions.explanation: The assessment values organized reasoning, not only numerical answers.
